name: Stats_NZ
description: Annual Enterprise Survey – Industry Financial Performance (long-format NZSIOC extract)
author: Koru Studio

components: Sales, fees, rental and leasing income

readiness.method: End-to-end run of DashboardAgents.ReportAgent.Api/python_agent's generate_generic_report.py (match + build_report + row_export) against 4 real reference extracts, immediately after fixing dataContract from a broken multi-table shape (hardcoded sheet name 'annual-enterprise-survey-2025-financial-year-provisional', which no CSV upload could ever match -- see notes) to the proven single-table rowFields shape.
notes: Confirmed live row data now injects correctly for all 4 files (row counts exactly match each source file -- no truncation, no fallback to embedded mock data), which is the direct fix for the 'every upload looks the same' symptom: the prior multi-table dataContract always failed to find its hardcoded sheet name for any CSV upload, so row_export.export_row_data_multi() returned an empty array and chrome.html's init() silently fell back to its static MOCK_DATA every time regardless of input.

nz_aes_1yr_baseline.csv's datasetIntegrityMatchPct (50.0) sits exactly at DATASET_INTEGRITY_BLOCK_BELOW_PCT's floor -- it still renders (the gate is strict '<', not '<='), but with only 2 evaluable (group, identity) checks (a 1-year extract has little group diversity), this is the least statistically robust of the 4 and the most likely to flip to a block on a slightly different single-year sample. Worth a follow-up look rather than treating it as equally solid as the other 3.

All 4 files' integrity failures are the same shape: components sum to ~101-102% of target (a published-statistics rounding artifact, not a structural mapping error) -- consistent with the band's own upper bound (100.5%) being tuned against a different, larger reference sample than these 4 fixtures.
